info.scen_description: Patient Zero is infected with a previously dormant strain of Yersinia pestis from an unknown origin. Humanity must face a deadly bacterium that has been hidden for centuries - previously killing over 200 million people. However, the world has changed a lot in 700 years with better hygiene and more antibiotics.\nWill the disease be able to adapt and spread before its victims die off?
info.scen_init_popup1_title: Welcome to the Black Death scenario
info.scen_init_popup1_text: You are a new strain of the Black Death that has been uncovered. The world has changed a lot in 700 years though!

air_1.name: Air 1
air_1.description: Gives pathogen ability to travel on dust particles. Increase infectivity, especially in arid environments and plane transmission

air_2.name: Air 2
air_2.description: Gives organism ability to survive suspended in air for a long time. Increase infectivity, especially in arid environments and plane transmission

bird_1.name: Bird 1
bird_1.description: Birds become susceptible to infection. Avian carriers increase infectivity, land transmission and mutation

bird_2.name: Bird 2
bird_2.description: Avian brain tissue compromised causing birds to attack other species. Increases mutation, infectivity and land based transmission

blood_1.name: Blood 1
blood_1.description: Gives organism ability to spread through blood-to-blood contact. Increases infectivity, especially in poor regions and mutation chance

blood_2.name: Blood 2
blood_2.description: Infected bodily fluids able to pass through mucous membranes. Increases infectivity, especially in poor regions and mutation chance

livestock_1.name: Livestock 1
livestock_1.description: Livestock susceptible to infection. Increase infectivity, especially in rural regions and mutation

livestock_2.name: Livestock 2
livestock_2.description: Wildlife susceptible to infection.  Increase infectivity, especially in rural regions and mutation

extreme_zoonosis.name: Extreme Zoonosis
extreme_zoonosis.description: Infection crosses multiple species barriers. Increase infectivity, especially in rural and urban areas, mutation chance and cross-country transmission

extreme_bioaerosol.name: Extreme Bioaerosol
extreme_bioaerosol.description: Pathogen bypasses air/water filters due to adaptive cellular shell. Increase infectivity, especially in humid & arid climates and plane/ship transmission.

rodent_1.name: Rodent 1
rodent_1.description: Rodents directly susceptible to infection.  Increase infectivity, especially in urban regions and mutation

rodent_2.name: Rodent 2
rodent_2.description: Pathogen survives in rodent droppings. Infectivity increased, especially in urban regions

water_1.name: Water 1
water_1.description: Pathogen can survive outside the body in fresh, warm water. Increase infectivity, especially in humid environments and ship transmission

water_2.name: Water 2
water_2.description: Pathogen able to survive in chemically treated water. Increase infectivity, especially in humid environments and ship transmission

heat_resistance_1.name: Heat Resistance 1
heat_resistance_1.description: Pathogen evolves to withstand hot temperatures and climates

heat_resistance_2.name: Heat Resistance 2
heat_resistance_2.description: Pathogen avoids cellular breakdown in high temperatures. Increased effectiveness in hot climates

cold_resistance_1.name: Cold Resistance 1
cold_resistance_1.description: Pathogen evolves to withstand cold temperatures and climates

cold_resistance_2.name: Cold Resistance 2
cold_resistance_2.description: Lower intracellular water volume prevents freezing. Increased effectiveness in cold climates

environmental_hardening.name: Environmental Hardening
environmental_hardening.description: Pathogen develops hardened coating - becoming highly weather resistant and extremely comfortable in both hot and cold climates

drug_resistance_1.name: Drug Resistance 1
drug_resistance_1.description: Pathogen becomes resistant to class 1 and 2 antibiotics. Increase effectiveness in wealthy countries

drug_resistance_2.name: Drug Resistance 2
drug_resistance_2.description: Pathogen develops resistance to class 3 and 4 antibiotics. Increase effectiveness in wealthy countries

genetic_reshuffle_1.name: Genetic ReShuffle 1
genetic_reshuffle_1.description: Pathogen DNA strands reassembled. More work needed to develop a cure

genetic_reshuffle_2.name: Genetic ReShuffle 2
genetic_reshuffle_2.description: A new strain of the pathogen now exists, increasing the work needed to develop a cure

genetic_reshuffle_3.name: Genetic ReShuffle 3
genetic_reshuffle_3.description: Multiple strains of the pathogen now exist, increasing the work needed to develop a cure

genetic__hardening_1.name: Genetic Hardening 1
genetic__hardening_1.description: Pathogen becomes harder to analyse in the lab. Decreases future research speed

genetic__hardening_2.name: Genetic Hardening 2
genetic__hardening_2.description: The pathogen does not reproduce in lab conditions. Decreases future research speed

nausea.name: Nausea
nausea.description: Irritated stomach lining leads to discomfort. Slight chance of infection when kissing

coughing.name: Coughing
coughing.description: Chance of infection by spreading pathogen into surroundings, especially in high density, urban areas

cysts.name: Cysts
cysts.description: Painful lumps containing pockets of the pathogen. Slight chance of bursting which can spread disease

rash.name: Rash
rash.description: The skin becomes blistered and painful, slightly increasing infectivity

vomiting.name: Vomiting
vomiting.description: The expulsion of infected material through projectile vomiting increases the risk of infection

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.description: Serious fluid buildup and discharge from the lungs. People in cold climates especially vulnerable

hyper_sensitivity.name: Hyper sensitivity
hyper_sensitivity.description: Increases likelihood of allergic reactions which can distract the immune system. Rich regions particularly vulnerable

sneezing.name: Sneezing
sneezing.description: Fluid discharge through sneezing greatly increases infection rates

abscesses.name: Abscesses
abscesses.description: Pockets of infected flesh are painful and act as  breeding grounds for the pathogen, increasing infection rates when burst

sweating.name: Sweating
sweating.description: The loss of fluid through sweating also increases infection rates due to poor hygiene. More dangerous in cold countries

diarrhoea.name: Diarrhoea
diarrhoea.description: Pathogen active in digestive tract, causing infection through faeces and potentially lethal dehydration. Poor countries v. vulnerable

seizures.name: Seizures
seizures.description: Random blackouts and fits reduce the patient's ability to function independently. Can be fatal

pulmonary_oedema.name: Pulmonary Oedema
pulmonary_oedema.description: Potentially fatal heart abnormality causes breakdown of respiratory system, releasing pathogen into the air

inflammation.name: Inflammation
inflammation.description: Inflammation obstructs bodily processes. Swelling can obstruct breathing and be fatal

paralysis.name: Paralysis
paralysis.description: Pathogen destroys motor neurons to cause paralysis. Significantly harder to cure and can be lethal

immune_suppression.name: Immune Suppression
immune_suppression.description: Pathogens attach to lymphocytes, suppressing immune system and allowing significantly greater freedom of mutation. Can be lethal

systemic_infection.name: Systemic Infection
systemic_infection.description: Pathogen affects multiple organs and tissue types, causing body-wide infections that spread fast and can be fatal

fever.name: Fever
fever.description: Increase in temperature, contagiousness and severe dehydration, which can be fatal

skin_lesions.name: Skin Lesions
skin_lesions.description: Breakdown in the epidermis causes large open wounds which significantly increase infectivity

internal_haemorrhaging.name: Internal Haemorrhaging
internal_haemorrhaging.description: Arterial membranes break down, causing rapid internal bleeding and death

dysentery.name: Dysentery
dysentery.description: A complete breakdown in the digestive system causes infected sewage, dehydration, starvation and death

total_organ_failure.name: Total Organ Failure
total_organ_failure.description: Catastrophic cell death of multiple tissue types causes body-wide organ failure and rapid death

coma.name: Coma
coma.description: Neuropathic effects in the brain stem cause loss of consciousness and sometimes death. Significantly harder to cure

necrosis.name: Necrosis
necrosis.description: Large swathes of infected tissue lose blood supply and become fatal sources of gangrene. Decomposed bodies remain a vector of transmission

hemorrhagic_shock.name: Hemorrhagic Shock
hemorrhagic_shock.description: Severe loss of blood volume causes oxygen deprivation, loss of consciousness and death

bubonic_plague.name: Bubonic plague
bubonic_plague.description: Gain ability to infect lymphatic system and develop bubonic form of plague. Zoonotic and lethal

pneumonic_plague.name: Pneumonic plague
pneumonic_plague.description: Gain ability to infect respiratory system and develop pneumonic form of plague. Airborne and virulent

septicemic_plague.name: Septicemic plague
septicemic_plague.description: Gain ability to infect the bloodstream and develop septicemic form of plague. Rare and very lethal

drug_resistance_3.name: Drug Resistance 3
drug_resistance_3.description: Pathogen highly resistant to all known antibiotics. Harder to develop a cure

hardened_reshuffle_1.name: Hardened Reshuffle 1
hardened_reshuffle_1.description: Pathogen DNA structure reassembled and highly unstable. Significantly harder to develop cure and also slows research speed

hardened_reshuffle_2.name: Hardened Reshuffle 2
hardened_reshuffle_2.description: Pathogen DNA structure reassembled and highly unstable. Significantly harder to develop cure and also slows research speed

flea_1.name: Flea 1
flea_1.description: Common flea susceptible to infection.  Increase infectivity, especially in urban regions and mutation

flea_2.name: Flea 2
flea_2.description: Flea bites less likely to cause adverse reaction in host - increasing infectivity

flea_3.name: Flea 3
flea_3.description: Pathogen produces exotoxin that kills most infected fleas - reducing infectivity. However survivors resistant to synthetic insecticides

flea_4.name: Flea 4
flea_4.description: Pathogen exotoxin accelerates the flea life cycle - significantly reducing egg and larva susceptibility to extreme climates

hypotension.name: Hypotension
hypotension.description: Low blood pressure deprives organs of oxygen and nutrients, increasing severity and causing profound fatigue

haemoptysis.name: Haemoptysis
haemoptysis.description: Coughing up blood from inflamed bronchi increases infectivity and is fatal in extreme cases

buboes.name: Buboes
buboes.description: Infected lymph nodes become swollen and inflamed. Bursting can aerosolise contents and infect others
